title: Determinants of age at menarche in the UK: analyses from the Breakthrough Generations Study.
ehr_evidence: Age at menarche data were collected retrospectively by questionnaire from 81 606 women aged 16 – 98, resident in the UK and participating in the Breakthrough Generations Study.
summary: Cohort study investigating determinants of age at menarche using self-reported questionnaire data from over 80,000 UK women.
key_findings: Menarche occurred earlier in women with low birthweight (Ptrend < 0.001), singletons (P < 0.001), prenatal pre-eclampsia (P < 0.001) or maternal smoking (P = 0.01), not breastfed (Ptrend = 0.03), non-white (P < 0.001), heavy or tall at age 7 (Ptrend < 0.001), and those who exercised little (Ptrend < 0.001).
Menarcheal age increased with number of siblings (P < 0.001) and had an inverse association with birth order (P < 0.001).
In the multivariate model, birthweight, ethnicity, weight, height, exercise, sibship size, birth order, and maternal age at birth remained significant.

A non-white girl who was much heavier and taller than peers at age 7 could reach menarche nearly 2 years earlier on average (difference = -22.8 months, 95% CI = -25.0 to -20.7 months) compared to a white girl of average weight and height.
Birthweight per 500 g increase was associated with 0.31 months later menarche in univariate analysis and 1.24 months in multivariate analysis.
No significant association was found with maternal age at birth in univariate analysis (Ptrend = 0.15) or vegetarian status before age 8 (P = 0.18).
exposure_domain: prenatal and early-life factors (birthweight, maternal smoking, pre-eclampsia, breastfeeding, childhood anthropometrics, exercise, family size, birth order, ethnicity, maternal age)
limitations: retrospective self-reported data with recall error
imprecise measures of childhood weight and height
large amounts of missing data for breastfeeding and maternal smoking variables
